items.plain: MongoDB Server lets anyone on the network crash database servers during a failover, and possibly run code; upgrade every replica set member now.
items.summary: A use-after-free in MongoDB Server's replication code can be triggered by unauthenticated requests when a newly elected replica set primary completes catch-up, crashing the server or possibly running code in the server process. Fixed releases are out for all supported branches — upgrade every replica set member to 9.0.7, 8.3.16, 8.0.37, 7.0.48, 6.0.30, 5.0.35 or 4.4.32.

items.plain: Red Hat Quay lets an attacker who creates a specially named account read other customers' private container login tokens; upgrade Quay now.
items.summary: Quay builds a database search pattern from user-controlled namespace names without escaping wildcard characters, so an attacker who creates a namespace containing an underscore can match and retrieve other tenants' robot accounts and their decrypted authentication tokens. Red Hat has released fixed Quay versions — upgrade to a patched release.

items.plain: Google Chrome lets a malicious web page break out of the browser's safety sandbox and run code on your computer; update Chrome now.
items.summary: Incorrect authorization in Chrome's FileSystem lets a remote attacker who tricks a user into visiting a crafted page run code outside the browser sandbox. Google fixed it in Chrome 157.0.8103.78 — update Chrome now.

items.plain: FortiOS lets a connected network peer send crafted routing data that corrupts routers across the network; apply Fortinet's November patches now.
items.summary: A numeric truncation error in FortiOS BGP lets a configured iBGP neighbor send malformed attributes that propagate to all connected routers, tampering with routing data. Fortinet's November advisory lists fixed releases — upgrade FortiOS 7.2, 7.4, 7.6 and 8.0.

items.plain: FortiOS lets an attacker without a login inject false routing messages into the network; apply Fortinet's November patches now.
items.summary: An authentication bypass in the FortiOS OSPF daemon lets an unauthenticated attacker broadcast crafted link-state advertisements, injecting false routing information. Fortinet's November advisory lists fixed releases — upgrade FortiOS 7.2, 7.4, 7.6 and 8.0.
